I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the most familiar system here, it fits my land and water conditions, and I understand how to manage it without taking extra risk. At the start of this season, the winter wheat is already in the ground, so my first job is to manage that crop carefully through spring with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and limited pesticide use only when needed. After wheat harvest in early summer, I will quickly sow summer maize on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want steadier yield and better stress tolerance, but I will not push fertilizer too hard because inputs are expensive and I want a reliable return, not the highest possible risk. I will use rotary tillage between crops because it is fast and practical for double-cropping. My whole plan is to keep the work simple, familiar, and stable, with wheat for security and maize for the main summer yield.
